NEW DELHI: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh will visit Dushanbe, Tajikistan, on October 19 and 20 to represent India at the 25th meeting of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation’s (SCO) Council of Heads of Government.According to news agency ANI, citing the Ministry of Defence, the meeting will focus on strengthening multilateral cooperation among SCO member states in trade, economy, investment, connectivity, innovation and cultural-humanitarian exchanges. The participating countries are also expected to review ongoing cooperation initiatives and consider decisions related to the organisation’s financial and institutional functioning.The agenda is expected to cover trade and investment cooperation, transport and logistics, industrial cooperation, the creative and digital economy, innovation and financial interaction, according to Interfax, which cited the Russian trade mission in Tajikistan. Social and cultural-humanitarian cooperation is also expected to feature in the discussions.India has highlighted the need to expand intra-SCO trade, lower trade costs, strengthen supply chains and improve connectivity.At a meeting of SCO ministers responsible for foreign economic and trade activities in Dushanbe in September, India called for simplified customs procedures, paperless trade, electronic document exchange and stronger multimodal connectivity, according to the Ministry of Commerce and Industry.India also highlighted opportunities for cooperation in agriculture, critical minerals, pharmaceuticals, manufacturing, electronics, energy security, renewable energy and green hydrogen. It called for greater use of digital and cross-border payments and improved access to trade finance for micro, small and medium enterprises and start-ups.The October meeting will provide India an opportunity to exchange views with other SCO member states on advancing practical and mutually beneficial cooperation. India remains actively engaged in SCO mechanisms and contributes to regional cooperation through initiatives in start-ups and innovation, digital public infrastructure and people-to-people exchanges, the Ministry of Defence said.The Council of Heads of Government adopts the SCO’s budget and addresses key issues related to cooperation within the organisation, particularly in the economic sphere. The body meets annually and is distinct from the Council of Heads of State, which serves as the organisation’s highest decision-making forum.The previous meeting of the Council of Heads of Government was held in Moscow on November 18, 2025, where India was represented by external affairs minister S Jaishankar, according to ANI.
Article Summary: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh will visit Dushanbe, Tajikistan, on October 19 and 20. He will represent India at the 25th meeting of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation’s (SCO) Council of Heads of Government. The meeting will focus on strengthening multilateral cooperation.

Article Title: AI cuts job demand in exposed occupations by nearly 10% across Asia: IMF report
Article Text:
As Job Placements Near, India Inc Taps Old IITs for AI Roles

AI creates demand for new skills

India faces jobs and skills challenge

Education, reskilling key to managing AI disruption

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping labour demand across Asia, with employer demand falling by nearly 10% in occupations more exposed to the technology since the launch of ChatGPT in November 2022, according to the International Monetary Fund’s (IMF) October 2026 Regional Economic Outlook: Asia and Pacific.The report, based on approximately 40 million online job postings across 19 Asian economies, highlights the challenges facing countries such as India, Indonesia and the Philippines as they seek to create productive jobs for growing working-age populations while AI transforms the sectors expected to absorb new workers.However, the decline in demand for workers in AI-exposed occupations appears to have stabilised, suggesting that the technology’s impact on employment is not limited to job displacement.The IMF report points to the emergence of new employment opportunities requiring specialised AI skills, including prompt engineering, retrieval-augmented generation and AI agent development.Employers are increasingly seeking workers who can integrate AI into business processes, improve productivity and translate technological capabilities into practical applications.Firm-level adoption of AI, however, remains uneven. Around 6% of firms in Asia explicitly seek AI skills in their job postings, the report said.Businesses adopting AI are experiencing stronger labour demand growth than those that have not adopted the technology, including in occupations highly exposed to automation. This suggests that AI can complement human capabilities even as it reduces demand for certain tasks.The implications of AI differ across Asian economies. Emerging economies such as India may initially be less exposed to the technology because a large share of their workforce remains employed in agriculture and other sectors less affected by AI.However, this could pose a longer-term challenge if AI makes it harder for workers to transition into higher-productivity manufacturing and services, the report said.For countries with expanding working-age populations, the challenge is to generate enough productive employment while ensuring that workers have the skills required by an increasingly technology-driven economy.The report emphasises that the response to AI must go beyond encouraging technological adoption. Education reform, reskilling programmes, digital infrastructure and stronger labour-market institutions will be essential to prepare workers for changing occupational demands.Businesses will also need to invest in workforce development alongside AI adoption to help employees adapt to new roles and changing skill requirements.The report suggests that AI need not become a barrier to inclusive growth. With timely investments in skills and preparedness, Asian economies could use the technology to boost productivity, encourage innovation and support sustainable employment.
Article Summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping labour demand across Asia. Employer demand has fallen by nearly 10% in occupations more exposed to the technology since the launch of ChatGPT in November 2022. The IMF report points to the emergence of new employment opportunities requiring specialised AI skills.

Article Title: FSSAI may curb sugar in baby food, set pesticide caps for tea
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has proposed two changes to food safety rules: prohibiting the addition of sucrose and fructose to products meant for babies up to six months and setting maximum residue limits for two pesticides in tea.The draft amendments were published in the Gazette of India on Oct 16. Currently, lactose and glucose polymers are the preferred carbohydrate sources in infant foods. Sucrose and fructose can be added when needed, but their combined amount cannot exceed 20% of total carbohydrates. The proposed amendment seeks to prohibit their addition in products for babies up to six months.The proposal aims to limit early exposure to added sugars amid concerns over childhood obesity and related health risks. It also complements recommendations for exclusive breastfeeding during the first six months. A doctor said the restriction must be enforced at the licensing stage. “FSSAI should also consider extending the ban to products intended for children above six months, given concerns over obesity.FSSAI has also proposed maximum residue limits of 20 parts per million (ppm) for acetamiprid and 50 ppm for imidacloprid in tea.Maxim­um residue limits specify the highest legally permitted co­n­­centration of pesticide residues in food and provide ben­chmarks. They do not indicate the amount necessarily pr­esent in a particular sample.One doctor said the proposed limits need to be accompanied by realistic assessments of consumer exposure. “Since tea is consumed several times a day, it is important to assess how much of these chemicals passes from the leaves into the brewed drink.”
Article Summary: The draft amendments were published in the Gazette of India on Oct 16. Currently, lactose and glucose polymers are the preferred carbohydrate sources in infant foods. The proposed amendment seeks to prohibit their addition in products for babies up to six months. The proposal aims to limit early exposure to added sugars amid concerns over childhood obesity.

Article Title: FSSAI cracks down on Priyagold biscuit maker
Article Text:
The FSSAI has taken legal action against three companies over serious violations of food safety standards

NEW DELHI: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has stepped up enforcement against major food companies, sanctioning prosecution against Priyagold biscuit maker Surya Food & Agro Ltd, Dodla Dairy Ltd and Ueir Organic Foods Pvt Ltd, while issuing notices to Nestlé India and Hindustan Unilever (HUL) over alleged labelling violations and misleading product claims.Action against Surya Food & Agro followed a consumer complaint that led officials to find bran meant for cattle feed being used as a fibre source in Priyagold biscuits.The gunny bags containing the material for the biscuits were marked for cattle feed. Inspectors also flagged deficiencies in plant hygiene, pest control, raw material storage and segregation, personnel hygiene and premises maintenance. The company’s FSSAI licence was suspended following the inspection, and the competent authority has now sanctioned prosecution. Attempts to reach the company for comment were unsuccessful.FSSAI has issued notices to Nestlé India over its Nescafé ready-to-drink range, including Cappuccino, Choco Mocha and Chilled Latte, manufactured by Schreiber Dynamix Dairies and Lotus Dairy Products. The regulator flagged discrepancies between the front-of-pack description “Flavoured Milk” and the back label, which classified the products as “Proprietary Food – 1.12 Dairy Based Drink”.Online listings described them as “Coffee Flavoured Milk” and carried claims about the goodness of flavoured double-toned milk, which FSSAI said were inconsistent with the declared product category. The companies have been asked to explain why action should not be initiated under food safety laws.A separate notice to Nestlé concerned its Resource Renal vanilla flavour powder, intended for dietary management of people with conservatively treated chronic kidney disease. FSSAI said the product lacked the required prior approval and that the prescribed vegetarian or non-vegetarian symbol was missing from the label.In a statement the company said, “FSSAI has sent a communication to Nestlé India concerning the label declarations/classification of the Nescafe Ready To Drink products. This does not relate to product safety or product quality. Mentioned products are safe to consume and meet all applicable food safety requirements.We will be submitting our response to the authorities and will be engaging with them as per due process established under law. ” Hindustan Unilever was issued notices over claims on Horlicks Women’s Plus Chocolate Nutrition Drink, including “Nutrition for Strong Bones” and “Clinically Proven to Help Improve Bone Strength in 6 Months”.In a statement to the press, the company spokesperson said, “Hindustan Unilever Limited is committed to providing safe, high-quality products that comply with all applicable regulatory requirements. Horlicks Women’s Plus and Mother’s Plus has been developed based on established nutritional science and is manufactured in accordance with stringent quality and safety standards. All product communication is developed in accordance with applicable laws, regulations, and governance processes. We will share all the scientific and regulatory evidence with the authorities as per normal process of review.”
Article Summary: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has stepped up enforcement against major food companies. The regulator has sanctioned prosecution against Priyagold biscuit maker Surya Food & Agro Ltd, Dodla Dairy Ltd and Ueir Organic Foods Pvt Ltd. It has also issued notices to Nestlé India and Hindustan Unilever over alleged labelling violations and misleading product claims.

NEW DELHI: The promised nonstop drive between Delhi and Mumbai may have to wait until Dec 2029, with the govt’s flagship Delhi-Mumbai Expressway running more than five years behind its original deadline. Work on three sections, spanning around 90 km, of the high-speed corridor in Gujarat is yet to start, with NHAI processing bids for two sections, including one where the last successful bidder withdrew from the project, forfeiting Rs 15 crore of bid security.The process of appointing a replacement contractor for the third section is in its final stage.The three packages in Gujarat -- package 8, 9 and 10 -- were earlier awarded to Pune-based highway developer Roadways Solutions India Infra Ltd (RSIIL), but the contracts were terminated as it failed to meet the set milestones despite getting multiple extensions, NHAI officials said.They said that for package-8 (Jujuwa to Gandewa), NHAI has received seven bids and for package 9 (Karvad to Jujuwa), there are six bids. NHAI had to go for fresh bids for package-8 after the last successful bidder, Bansal Construction Works, did not sign the Letter of Acceptance (LoA) “without quoting any reason”. TOI has learnt that officials were surprised to find that the company raised no issues and forfeited the bid security amount, which is unheard of in NHAI’s recent history.People aware of the development said RSIIL, which has been blacklisted by NHAI from bidding for projects following non-performance, has submitted a bid for package-9. Officials said that though RSIIL has moved court against NHAI’s eligibility criteria, which exclude it from bidding, Delhi High Court has green-lighted NHAI’s evaluation of the bids. The matter is scheduled to come up for hearing next week.Officials said they are confident of completing the process this month so that work can start in the next couple of months. They added that the construction work would take around two years. “These three stretches would be ready latest by December 2029. The Expressway project has faced delay due to several reasons, including Covid-19, delay in land acquisition and statutory approvals,” said one of them.People involved in the project said that apart from the three sections in Gujarat, one stretch each in Maharashtra and Rajasthan is yet to be completed. These two sections would be ready by April 2027.Govt had promised to bring down the travel time between Delhi and Mumbai by half to barely 12 hours through the expressway.
Article Summary: The promised nonstop drive between Delhi and Mumbai may have to wait until Dec 2029. The govt’s flagship Delhi-Mumbai Expressway running more than five years behind its original deadline. Work on three sections, spanning around 90 km, of the high-speed corridor in Gujarat is yet to start.

Article Title: Prices of 137 cancer drugs to fall by up to 70% from November 9
Article Text:
This follows a nudge by Supreme Court, flagging the huge gap between price to retailer and MRP of medicines billed to patients

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

In good news for cancer patients, prices of 137 drugs are set to be reduced by up to 70% from Nov 9, with govt capping trade margins by 30%. Drug prices regulator National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA) Saturday notified the 137 non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs to address the issue of excessive trade margins, invoking Paragraph 19 of DPCO, 2013. Significantly, patented drugs are also included in the list.The trade margin rationalisation at 30% of MRP, excluding GST, corresponds to a mark-up of 42.9% on price to stockist/price to distributor (PTS/PTD), according to the minutes of the NPPA meeting accessed by TOI. Simply put, PTS/PTD is the first point of sale of the drug.This follows a nudge by Supreme Court, flagging the huge gap between price to retailer and MRP of medicines billed to patients, in certain cases of 10 times.The MRPs of certain drugs — including pertuzumab + trastuzumab, atezolizumab, teclistamab, inotuzumab ozogamicin and daratumumab — are up to Rs 5 lakh per vial/pack.All manufacturers will be required to inform NPPA of their revised prices within seven days of publication of the gazette notification. Manufacturers will be req-uired to display the price lists on their website and widely disseminate them to all retailers and hospitals, with the latter also required to display the revised prices on their websites prominently.The authority approved the calculation of the revised MRP based on PTS/PTD for March 2026 as the reference month.NPPA said patient assistance programme quantities may be excluded from the calculation of PTS/PTD and MRP for trade-margin capping only. These programmes, where drugs are supplied free of cost, are typically run by MNCs.As a substantial supply of anti-cancer drugs is directly made to hospitals and medical institutions, they shall be responsible for ensuring revised prices of such drugs from the date of implementation, NPPA said. State drug controllers will take necessary steps to ensure compliance by manufacturers, dealers including retailers, hospitals and medical institutions, it added.In a bid to tighten rules further, NPPA said uninterrupted availability of the covered formulations needed to be ensured. Any manufacturer intending to reduce monthly production levels would have to obtain permission.Consumers can use the Pharma Sahi Daam app and NPPA website to check revised prices of drugs, an official release said.In 2019, the MRP of 526 brands of non-scheduled anti-cancer medicines was reduced by up to 90%, NPPA said. The present exercise extends this approach to a larger set of drugs, based on the list recommended by an expert committee under Directorate General of Health Services.
Article Summary: National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA) Saturday notified the 137 non- scheduled anti-cancer drugs to address the issue of excessive trade margins. Significantly, patented drugs are also included in the list. This follows a nudge by Supreme Court, flagging the huge gap between price to retailer and MRP of medicines billed to patients.

Article Title: Internet is fundamental right of all, even children: Supreme Court
Article Text:
It said the efficacy of such restrictive measures remains far from established in countries which have imposed them.

SC: Internet’s value priceless, efficacy of curbs not proved

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Raising citizens’ right to access and use of internet to the level of fundamental right, Supreme Court has held that even children are entitled to that right and said it does not endorse imposing in the name of safety a blanket ban on children accessing internet. At the same time, it favoured restricting access to content that is inherently harmful to kids.A bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K V Chandran said that right to access and use of the internet is part of Article 21 (right to life and liberty) and Article 19(1)(a) (freedom of speech and expression). The internet is “priceless” as it provides access to information and education to all in even remote areas, where it is often the only source of learning for many children. Noting that the SC had earlier refrained from expressing a definitive view on whether the right to access the internet is, by itself, a fundamental right, the bench said, “. ..we have no hesitation in saying that the right to access and use the internet is a fundamental right of every individual under Article 21 read with Article 19(1)(a) of the Constitution.”SC said, “Our children, irrespective of their age enjoy the same rights, and to deny the same altogether would be as absurd as saying children below a certain age do not have a conscience worth protecting or freedom of speech worth expressing.”The order was passed on a public interest litigationfiled by NGO ‘Just Rights for Children Alliance’, which highlights continued lapses by intermediaries in tackling child sexual exploitation and abuse material (CSEAM) despite SC’s 2024 judgment in this regard.Agreeing with its plea, SC said there has been “no progress worth the name” in the last two years.Acknowledging that there has been “a growing yet short-lived tendency across the globe in the recent past to limit the access of children below a certain age to the internet, more particularly to social media platforms,” SC said, “we too gave this our anxious consideration, and only thereafter, we decided consciously not to endorse the same”.It said the efficacy of such restrictive measures remains far from established in countries which have imposed them.“... Children do not cease to use the internet merely because the law prohibits them from doing so ... They move to other platforms and websites that are unregulated and even more unsafe,” SC said.“All that we are trying to say is that any blanket restriction on access to internet by children is nothing more than unproven measures of proven disproportionality. No jurisdiction has, so far, been able to demonstrate that children are any safer on account of such measures,” it said.It said some age-based restrictions and safeguards should exist for the safety of children online.
Article Summary: A bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K V Chandran said that right to access and use of the internet is part of Article 21 (right to life and liberty) and Article 19(1)(a) (freedom of speech and expression) The internet is “priceless” as it provides access to information and education to all in even remote areas.

Article Title: NCB busts two synthetic drug labs in Greater Noida, seizes drugs worth Rs 50 crore
Article Text:

recovery of nearly 380 kg of amphetamine-containing material— encompassing crystalline, semi-crystalline, and liquid forms

The premises were heavily equipped with large-capacity heating mantles, glass reaction vessels, filtration machinery, and laboratory apparatus tailored for mass production.

NEW DELHI: In a significant crackdown on illicit drugs network in Delhi-NCR, the Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB) has busted two clandestine synthetic-drug manufacturing laboratories in Greater Noida, Uttar Pradesh, seizing a huge haul of Methamphetamine worth around Rs 50 crores, precursors and manufacturing equipment.Union home minister Amit Shah termed the operation as a 'major milestone'. "It is a remarkable example of intelligence-led enforcement and a testament to our commitment to eliminating drug cartels before December 2029," he said in a post on X.The raid, conducted under Op Crystal Hunt on Oct 16 2026 at village Jahanabad Kadalpur in Gautam Buddha Nagar, led to the recovery of nearly 380 kg of amphetamine-containing material— encompassing crystalline, semi-crystalline, and liquid forms — alongside 10 kg of pseudoephedrine and large quantities of precursor chemicals such as acetone, toluene, and hydrochloric acid.According to officials, the seized materials are projected to yield over 56 kg of finished crystalline amphetamine. The premises were heavily equipped with large-capacity heating mantles, glass reaction vessels, filtration machinery, and laboratory apparatus tailored for mass production.Two individuals have been arrested in connection with the operation. One suspect identified himself as Destiny Abraham Dumbiri, a Nigerian national.However, immigration checks revealed he entered India in January 2020 under the alias Francis Kalokoh using a tourist visa that expired in December of that year, underscoring the sophisticated tactics used by traffickers to evade law enforcement.The second accused, Ms Lallawmzuali, alias Olivia Lalchawimawii, a resident of Mizoram, was out on bail following an earlier arrest in March 2026 by the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence in Goa for allegedly possessing a commercial quantity of heroin.This latest operation builds upon the NCB's ongoing efforts to dismantle organized cartels, echoing a previous October 2024 raid in the Kasna Industrial Area that exposed suspected ties to the Mexican cartel Cártel de Jalisco Nueva Generación.Investigators are tracing the financial trails, chemical procurement channels, and broader distribution networks associated with the arrested pair to uncover further interstate and international links.Beyond the direct threat of narcotics, authorities emphasized the severe environmental and public health hazards posed by such hidden facilities, noting that the untreated discharge of chemical waste severely contaminates local soil, drainage systems, and water bodies.The NCB has issued a strong public appeal urging landlords, property dealers, housing societies, and Resident Welfare Associations to remain vigilant. "Citizens are encouraged to report suspicious indicators such as unusual chemical odors, unexplained storage of drums, or heavy lab equipment to the National Narcotics Helpline MANAS at 1933, reinforcing the nation's collective stride toward a Nasha Mukt Bharat," the NCB said.
Article Summary: The premises were heavily equipped with large-capacity heating mantles, glass reaction vessels, filtration machinery, and laboratory apparatus tailored for mass production. The raid led to the recovery of nearly 380 kg of amphetamine- containing material, alongside 10 kg of pseudoephedrine and large quantities of precursor chemicals.

Article Title: FSSAI proposes ban on added sugars in infant food for babies up to 6 months
Article Text:
FSSAI proposed to "prohibit the addition of sucrose and fructose in food products intended for infants up to six months of age." (Representative image: Baby food).

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India on Saturday proposed a ban on adding fructose and sucrose in food products for infants up to six months of age.The food regulator published a draft amendment called 'The draft Food Safety and Standards (Foods for Infant Nutrition) Amendment Regulations 2026' over the previous 2020 regulations, for public consultation. FSSAI proposed to "prohibit the addition of sucrose and fructose in food products intended for infants up to six months of age," the draft said.According to the proposal, Stakeholders can submit objections and suggestions within 60 days.The objective is to strengthen nutritional safeguards for infants, according to a statement from the ministry of health and family welfare, cited by PTI."The first six months of life represent a critical period for healthy growth and development, making appropriate nutrition particularly important. The proposed restriction seeks to ensure that infant nutrition products meet the nutritional needs of this age group without unnecessary addition of sucrose and fructose," the ministry said.The existing regulations set nutritional composition, quality and safety standards for infant nutrition products designed for children from birth to 24 months. They identify lactose and glucose polymers as the preferred carbohydrate sources, while allowing sucrose and fructose to be added, within prescribed limits, when needed to provide carbohydrates.The proposed amendment seeks to tighten these provisions by barring the addition of sucrose and fructose to products intended for infants up to six months of age.
Article Summary: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India proposed a ban on adding fructose and sucrose in food products for infants up to six months of age. Stakeholders can submit objections and suggestions within 60 days. The objective is to strengthen nutritional safeguards for infants, says the ministry of health and family welfare.

There is much mischief behind it," Ramesh said in a post on X, alleging that the move could compromise the credibility of the decennial exercise.The Congress leader linked the census notification to an RSS training camp held in Belgaum from July 10 to 12, 2026, which he claimed focused on Census 2027. He also flagged the high-level committee on demographic changes, constituted by the Union home ministry on May 26, 2026, which invited public inputs, including from Indian and foreign organisations, on October 14.“The only thing high level of this committee is the affiliation of its members to the RSS ecosystem. So we know where these inputs will come from,” Ramesh alleged.Calling the expansion a “Rozgar Guarantee Yojana for thousands of RSS/BJP workers”, he claimed it could further undermine the census process.“This will most certainly further contaminate an already subverted Census. Another institution is being destroyed. Like SIR, the Census will also be dangerously doctored,” he said.Also Read| Centre expands Census enumerator pool to include private school teachers, clerks The notification issued by Registrar General of India Mrityunjay Kumar Narayan specifically includes teachers from government, local authority, aided and unaided private institutions, societies and trusts.The amendment comes amid legal challenges to the deployment of private-school staff for census duties. The Punjab and Haryana high court and the Allahabad high court have granted interim relief in cases concerning the requisitioning of teachers from private institutions.Separately, the National Centre for Promotion of Employment for Disabled People (NCPEDP) has called for accessible and inclusive enumeration in Census 2027, urging clear information on the counting process, accessible self-enumeration facilities and sensitisation of census officials.“The Census 2027 will be the first decennial census since the enactment of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act, 2016, which recognises 21 types of disabilities,” the organisation said, according to news agency PTI.The 2027 Census, the eighth since Independence, will be conducted in two phases: house-listing and housing census, followed by population enumeration. Originally scheduled for 2021, the decennial exercise was postponed due to the Covid-19 pandemic, with the Union Cabinet approving Rs 11,718 crore for what is expected to be the country’s largest-ever headcount exercise.
Article Summary: Congress accuses Centre of pursuing a political agenda through expansion of pool of eligible enumerators for Census 2027. Party cites alleged links to an RSS training camp and a panel on demographic changes. Census Rules, 1990, allow states and Union territories to appoint teachers from aided and unaided private institutions.

Article Title: 'Internet access is fundamental right': SC suggests ‘child mode’ for social media accounts
Article Text:
Blanket restrictions are not the answer

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Building on earlier rulings

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Saturday declared access to and use of the internet a fundamental right for every individual, including children, under Articles 21 and 19(1)(a) of the Constitution, observing that “The safety of our children and their freedom are not at odds with each other. ”The bench of Justice JB Pardiwala and Justice K Vinod Chandran also suggested that children’s online safety should be strengthened through measures such as a ‘child mode’ for social media accounts, rather than denying them access to the internet altogether, LiveLaw reported.A bench comprising Justice JB Pardiwala and Justice K Vinod Chandran made the observations while issuing directions to strengthen mechanisms for detecting and removing child sexual exploitation and abuse material (CSEAM) from social media platforms and other online services.According to LiveLaw, the bench said: "..we have no hesitation in saying that the right to access and use the internet is a fundamental right of every individual under Article 21 read with Article 19(1)(a) of the Constitution. Our children, irrespective of their age enjoy the same rights, and to deny the same altogether would be as absurd as saying children below a certain age do not have a conscience worth protecting or a freedom of speech worth expressing.The safety of our children and their freedom are not at odds with each other. Our children are entitled to both."The bench acknowledged that the internet, in its present form, poses safety risks to children. However, it said restricting children's access because online platforms had failed to detect and remove harmful material would amount to mistaking the victim for the problem.The court examined whether children should be completely shielded from the internet and social media in the interest of their safety. It noted that the right to freedom of speech and expression under Article 19(1)(a) includes the right to know, receive and impart information and ideas.Describing the internet as a marketplace of ideas, creative expression and information, the court said its value extended beyond the material available online to the opportunities it provided for learning, communication and access to information."For many children, particularly in remote areas, it is often the only source of learning and information," the court observed.It also noted that the internet could be particularly important for children with special needs, for whom online platforms might be the only place to find companionship with others facing similar circumstances.The bench referred to the Supreme Court's 2020 judgment in Anuradha Bhasin v. Union of India, which held that "the freedom of speech and expression and the freedom to carry on any trade or business through the medium of the internet is constitutionally protected as a fundamental right under Article 19(1)(a) and 19(1)(g) of the Constitution."In that judgment, the court had refrained from expressing a view on whether the right to access the internet, by itself, constituted a fundamental right.The bench also referred to the 2025 judgment in Pragya Prasun & Ors. v. Union of India, in which the court recognised the right to digital access as a fundamental right under Article 21.
Article Summary: Supreme Court declares access to and use of the internet a fundamental right for every individual, including children. The court also suggested that children’s online safety should be strengthened through measures such as a ‘child mode’ for social media accounts.

NEW DELHI: A Delhi court has issued bailable warrants against YouTuber Dhruv Rathee in a 2018 defamation case, news agency PTI reported.The case stems from a video published by Rathee in May 2018, in which he allegedly claimed that the Bharatiya Janata Party’s ( BJP ) Information Technology cell had attempted to bribe a man to defame him. The video was posted on Rathee’s social media account and later retweeted by Arvind Kejriwal, who was then the Delhi chief minister.The complainant, Vikas Sankrityayan, also known as Vikas Pandey, subsequently initiated defamation proceedings against Rathee and Kejriwal over the video and its circulation.Earlier, on October 12, Judicial Magistrate Rahul Jain of the Saket court ordered fresh summons to Rathee after the complainant submitted that repeated attempts to serve him had remained unsuccessful since the proceedings began.The complainant’s counsel, advocate Samaksh Sharma, told the court that the summons had remained unserved for several years as Rathee primarily lived abroad. The court was informed, however, that Rathee was then in India and residing at an address in Gurugram, Haryana.The magistrate noted that Rathee had first been summoned on July 23, 2019, and that the complainant had continued to pursue service of the summons.The court allowed Pandey to accompany the process server and directed him to deposit the process fee within two days. The next hearing was scheduled for October 17, 2026.Separately, Rathee is facing a defamation suit before the Saket court over a video that allegedly claimed Lord Ram and Goddess Sita consumed meat and alcohol during their exile.The complainants, who identified themselves as Hindu devotees, alleged that the video hurt their religious sentiments. Article Title: ‘He spoke to Putin to buy diesel’: Ex-diplomat Fabian after Trump waives sanctions over Russian oil
Article Text:
"President Trump contradicts President Trump... what he says today is not what he might say tomorrow": Ex-diplomat Fabian

Trump pauses sanctions

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

What it means for India

NEW DELHI: Former diplomat KP Fabian on Saturday questioned the rationale behind the US tariff pressure on India over Russian oil purchases, arguing that Washington’s own decision to waive sanctions-related duties under the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act exposed a contradiction in its approach.His remarks came after US President Donald Trump earlier today waived sanctions-related duties under the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act.Speaking to ANI, Fabian said, “Trump himself spoke to Putin to buy diesel. If America itself is buying, either it should sanction itself, which is ridiculous."He also argued that the tariff threats against India were a negotiating tactic aimed at securing a favourable trade deal rather than a genuine response to New Delhi’s energy purchases from Russia.“Certain tariffs were imposed, and the court in the United States said that Trump had no business."Fabian said Trump had avoided directly confronting Chinese President Xi Jinping over Russian oil purchases because China was a major buyer of Russian exports and Washington wanted closer engagement with Beijing.“Contrary to the Lindsey Graham Act, President Trump did not dare to mention it to Xi Jinping because China is a top buyer, 50 per cent of Russia’s exports.India comes next at 37 per cent,” he told ANI.However, Trump earlier on Saturday paused provisions of the Graham Act that could have imposed tariffs of up to 100% on goods imported into the US from the five largest buyers of Russian crude oil or natural gas, including India and China.The move comes against the backdrop of rising diesel prices in the US ahead of the November midterm elections and a reported agreement under which Russia would supply diesel fuel to Washington.Trump invoked Section 115 of the Act, which authorises the US president to waive certain sanctions-related provisions and restrictions involving foreign entities.“I have submitted to the Congress a certification that the issuance of such a waiver is in the national interests of the United States and a report explaining the basis for the certification, consistent with section 115(b) of the Graham Act,” Trump said in the order.Russia continues to be the single largest supplier of oil for India. A waiver of tariffs of up to 100% which may have come into place in the coming days means that India can continue importing oil in large numbers from Moscow without any economic fallout.If 100% tariffs had been imposed by the Trump administration, then it would have hit exporters as the US is the largest trading partner for India. At the same time, any sanctions may have rendered Russian crude economically unviable which would have added to the supply crunch at a time when Middle East tensions continue.
Article Summary: Former diplomat KP Fabian questioned the rationale behind the US tariff pressure on India over Russian oil purchases. He argued that Washington’s own decision to waive sanctions-related duties under the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act exposed a contradiction in its approach. Fabian said the tariff threats against India were a negotiating tactic aimed at securing a favourable trade deal.

Article Title: Watch: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay launches one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns
Article Text:
Vijay presented 22-carat, one-gram gold rings to 25 newborns. (PTI)

Who is eligible for the gold ring?

Scheme draws on Tamil tradition

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. He also held some of the newborns and presented the rings to beneficiaries during the launch programme.Under the scheme, eligible babies born in government hospitals and government primary health centres will receive a 22-carat, one-gram gold ring.The initiative, named the Maternal Uncle Gold Ring Scheme (Thaaimaman Thanga Mothiram Thittam), has an annual allocation of Rs 755.83 crore.It is aimed at celebrating motherhood, promoting maternal and child health and encouraging institutional deliveries by increasing public confidence in government healthcare facilities.The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions.Mothers must be registered under the Pregnancy and Infant Cohort Monitoring and Evaluation (PICME) system and have a Reproductive and Child Health (RCH) ID. They will also have to provide an e-KYC-verified Aadhaar card along with one of the prescribed identity or residence documents.These include ration cards, voter identity cards, Labour Welfare Board identity cards, Department of Posts address cards and nativity certificates.The state government has already procured 1.28 lakh one-gram gold rings for the initial rollout. Each ring will have a unique serial number and will be packed in tamper-proof packaging.From Monday, babies born in government hospitals will receive the rings at the time of discharge, according to the state government.To clear the backlog of eligible babies born between June 22 and Monday, the government will distribute the rings through 107 hubs across Tamil Nadu.Distribution will begin at the rate of 100 babies per day at each hub. At designated centres, 25 beneficiaries will be accommodated in the morning and another 25 in the afternoon to avoid overcrowding, PTI reported.Village Health Nurses will distribute invitations informing beneficiaries of their allotted date and time. Beneficiaries have been asked to visit the designated centres only at the time mentioned in their invitations.The district administration has also made transportation arrangements for beneficiaries from their respective areas. Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election as a symbolic gift to newborns, drawing on the Tamil tradition of ‘Thaimaaman Seer’. The scheme has retrospective effect from June 22, Vijay’s birthday.A government order issued on June 23 described the initiative as a token celebrating the birth of a child, motherhood and the cultural tradition of ‘Thaimaaman’.According to ANI, Tamil Nadu minister Arun Raj explained the cultural significance of the initiative saying, "A maternal uncle is someone who is among the first to rush in when a child is born, sharing in his sister’s happiness as his own. He assures her that he will always stand by her and her child, offering love, support and a sense of security.""Today, the Tamil Nadu Government, under the leadership of our brother, Mr. Vijay, is embracing this sacred bond of the maternal uncle and, as a gesture of that affection, is set to provide a one-gram gold ring to every child born in government hospitals. When the scheme was announced and the question arose as to where it should be launched, the place chosen by our Chief Minister was Madurai. This is the sacred soil of Madurai, blessed with the compassion and grace of Mother Meenakshi," he added.Tamil Nadu records around 7.8 lakh deliveries annually, with institutional deliveries accounting for 99.9% of births, according to NFHS-6. Government health facilities account for nearly 4.2 lakh deliveries, or around 53% of the total.According to the state government, the average out-of-pocket expenditure for a delivery at a government hospital is Rs 1,364, compared with Rs 63,473 at a private hospital.The government said the scheme is intended to encourage safe institutional deliveries, strengthen maternal and child welfare and increase public trust in government healthcare services.The Tamil Nadu Medical Services Corporation will procure the gold rings based on annual requirements, while a project and programme management unit will oversee implementation and monitoring.
Article Summary: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions. Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election.

Article Title: Delhi landfill garbage mountains shrinking, 100 acres reclaimed in 18 months: CM Rekha Gupta
Article Text:
Delhi CM Rekha Gupta poses for a group picture during an on-site inspection of waste disposal operations near Okhla, in New Delhi

Government targets legacy and fresh waste

New processing plants at three sites

NEW DELHI: Delhi chief minister Rekha Gupta on Saturday said the garbage mountains at the city's landfill sites were steadily shrinking as she reviewed waste disposal work at Okhla and laid the foundation stone for new waste processing facilities at Okhla, Ghazipur and Singhola.Gupta said the Delhi government had reclaimed 100 acres of land across the city's three landfill sites over the past one-and-a-half years, with a large portion of the cleared area also being turned green.She said almost all legacy waste at Okhla that existed before January 2025 had been processed."Today, at Okhla, we have processed almost all the legacy waste that was there before January 2025," Gupta said.Gupta said the government was working on two fronts: clearing the existing garbage mountains while ensuring that fresh waste generated every day did not accumulate into new landfill sites.According to news agency ANI, she said around 3,000-4,000 metric tonnes of fresh waste reaches the sites daily and is being processed round the clock."The garbage currently piled up here is essentially fresh waste generated after January 2025, and that too is being processed round the clock. So, we are fighting on two fronts: one is eliminating waste, and the other is ensuring that the 3,000 to 4,000 metric tons of fresh waste arriving daily is processed immediately, so that new garbage mountains are not formed for future generations," Gupta said.She said the government was working to reduce the existing garbage mountains to zero."People are seeing that the garbage mountains are continuously shrinking and soon a time will come when they will become zero," Gupta said.Gupta also said she had taken what she described as her "last selfie" with the garbage mountain at Okhla."Today I have taken my last selfie with the garbage mountain; after this I have taken a pledge that this garbage mountain will end soon," she said.Taking a jibe at the Opposition, Gupta added, "I had said - garbage mountain, you will have to go; the opposition mocked. Today I will say the garbage mountain is going; now only its back remains."During the programme at the Okhla SLF site, Gupta laid the foundation stone for fresh waste processing plants at Okhla, Ghazipur and Singhola, as well as a biogas facility at Ghazipur. She also inaugurated the M&CW Centre at Kotla Mubarakpur through virtual mode from Okhla.The Okhla plant will be built at a cost of Rs 103 crore and will have a processing capacity of 1,400 metric tonnes per day.The Singhola facility will cost Rs 42 crore and have a capacity of 800 metric tonnes per day, while the Ghazipur plant will have a processing capacity of 700 metric tonnes per day.The facilities are intended to process fresh waste as well as construction and demolition waste. Gupta said the new units would also produce biogas, green energy and manure."Waste should not remain waste; Delhi should use it as wealth," she said, adding that new technologies were being introduced for waste segregation and processing.She said waste and cattle dung would be used to produce biogas and manure as part of efforts to build a technology-driven waste management system.Gupta said the government was taking up several measures to address pollution, including work on landfill waste, cleaning the Yamuna, dust mitigation, plantation, road infrastructure and waste management."Our government is tackling pollution from a 360-degree perspective to ensure it gradually decreases. We are working on every aspect, be it addressing the mountains of garbage, cleaning the Yamuna, improving road infrastructure, or managing waste, to ensure the people of Delhi enjoy better air quality. Our resolve and policies are absolutely clear, and we are working 24x7 in the public interest," she said.The chief minister also reviewed the progress of waste disposal work with officials and directed them to accelerate the work according to the stipulated timeline.She said the garbage mountains at Bhalswa, Ghazipur and Okhla had caused inconvenience to people travelling through these areas and said the government was continuing efforts to eliminate them.
Article Summary: Gupta said the Delhi government had reclaimed 100 acres of land across the city's three landfill sites over the past one-and-a-half years. She said almost all legacy waste at Okhla that existed before January 2025 had been processed. Gupta said the new units would also produce biogas, green energy and manure.

Article Title: India-US trade talks hit ‘plateau’: Sitharaman says further give-and-take ‘very, very difficult’
Article Text:
Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman

India stresses strategic autonomy in trade negotiations

India-EU pact opens market access

India and US have reached a “plateau” in negotiations over their bilateral trade agreement, with further concessions from either side likely to be "very very difficult", finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman said on Monday. Speaking at the Munich Leaders Meeting in New Delhi, she said that while negotiations are still underway, any progress from here would depend on whether there was limited room for compromise on either side.“The agreement negotiations are still ongoing, although we'd like to believe that both the sides have reached a plateau beyond which giving or taking might be very, very difficult. But maybe if there are rooms to operate from, both sides would do it,” Sitharaman said.She said the agreement was still being “hard and very rigorously negotiated” and that India has a trade surplus with the US. “But what is the predominant feature of the trade relations between India and the US? The trade balance is very much in our favor.”Sitharaman said that the US would naturally want to reduce this trade imbalance and address what it sees as losses built up over the years.She also said that the way countries negotiate trade deals was changing, with governments now looking beyond traditional negotiations to address trade imbalances.“Negotiation used to be the only platform through which countries could highlight the discrepancies, highlight the lop-sidedness and say, would we want to correct this?” she said.“Tariff was an instrument of negotiation, and tariff had a certain framework within which you will apply it. Today framework is there, tariffs are going,” she said, while stressing that countries still need to negotiate and find “some give and take”.Sitharaman was also asked about maintaining strategic autonomy while negotiating bilateral trade agreements with European countries, including in the context of India procuring Russian oil."There is no Lindsay Graham Bill in Europe...," she said.On the broader question of how bilateral trade agreements can protect a country's interests in an era of multilateralism, Sitharaman said countries were increasingly choosing bilateral partnerships where they saw greater benefit.“Countries choose where multilateralism would benefit them, and there are some unique bilaterals which countries choose to have. The balance is somewhat tilted in favour of the bilateral rather than the multilateral,” she said.She said countries were now increasingly looking for new trade partners and strengthening those relationships through agreements.“Countries are now rapidly catching up with — I would put the EU-India also in a bilateral mode -because it's one in the name of union, but of course within them they have. So, bilaterals today are catching up far more than even initiating or beginning a multilateral. It's not deliberate, but in a way, if you don't do it, you're not moving forward. Countries will have to choose new partners for their trade and strengthen the tie through an agreement. And therefore, newer partnerships are being searched for, and they are tied up bilaterally.”FM Sitharaman cited the India-EU trade agreement as a major example of India's approach to negotiating trade pacts while protecting domestic interests.She said India had opened 92.5 per cent of its tariff lines and around 97 per cent of tariff value under the agreement. The EU, meanwhile, had opened 99 per cent in value terms and possibly 97 per cent of tariff lines.According to Sitharaman, greater access to the European market could support employment in labour-intensive sectors, including footwear, textiles, toys and processed products. Many of these sectors are linked to micro and small enterprises.“Those are all in the micro and small medium industry segment, which are labor-intensive,” Sitharaman said, adding that greater access to the European market could generate “more exports, more jobs”.Sitharaman said bilateral trade agreements were becoming increasingly important as multilateral institutions have weakened.“Multilateralism is not going to go away. But multilateralism has weakened,” she said.She also stressed that multilateralism should continue even as countries increasingly pursue bilateral agreements.“Multilateralism is not going to go away and multilateralism shouldn't go away,” Sitharaman said.The Munich Leaders Meeting, being held in the National Capital, provides a platform for about 100 senior decision-makers and experts to discuss opportunities for stronger cooperation among emerging and middle powers amid profound geopolitical change. Discussions include geoeconomic developments, trade and connectivity, maritime security, defence cooperation and other key international challenges.
Article Summary: Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman says India and US have reached a 'plateau' in negotiations over their bilateral trade agreement. She said any progress from here would depend on whether there was limited room for compromise on either side. She also said the way countries negotiate trade deals was changing, with governments now looking beyond traditional negotiations to address trade imbalances.

Article Title: LPG consumption down, diesel & petrol sales up in September
Article Text:
LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier

NEW DELHI: LPG demand fell by over 9% year-on-year in Sept, while petrol and diesel sales registered growth of 7% and 5%, respectively, provisional data released by the Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell (PPAC) showed.LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier.Month-on-month consumption, however, registered a growth of 8%, up from 2.4 MT.Petrol sales increased from 3.4 MT in Sept last year to 3.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose from 6.8 MT to 7.1 MT. Petrol and diesel consumption had registered year-on-year growth of 7.9% and 6.5%, respectively, in July.While petrol is largely used as an automobile fuel and its consumption is commensurate with the increasing number of vehicles, diesel is consumed by transport vehicles for passenger and freight movement, besides being used in the agricultural sector.Erratic monsoon conditions due to El Nino boosted demand for diesel for irrigation.Cumulative petrol consumption during Apr-Sept in the current financial year increased 7% to 22.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose 4.8% to 47.9 MT. In contrast, LPG consumption declined 14.9% to 13.8 MT from 16.2 MT during the corresponding period of 2025-26.
Article Summary: LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier. Petrol sales increased from 3.4 MT in Sept last year to 3.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose from 6.8 MT to 7.1 MT.
