Article Title: Trump waives US sanctions, tariffs on Russian oil & gas - what it means for India
Article Text:
Trump announced the waiver just days before several provisions of the legislation were due to take effect.

What Trump announced

What it means for India

Competing for oil with China

In what is being seen as a big relief for India and China, US President Donald Trump has waived sanctions, restrictions and duties provided for under the Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act, citing the national interest of the United States.The Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 gave Trump the authority to impose broad sanctions on Russia and levy steep tariffs on major buyers of Russian oil and gas, including China and India.The legislation, principally backed in Congress by the late Senator Lindsey Graham, provided for tariffs of up to 100% within 30 days on goods entering the US from the five largest importers of Russian crude oil or gas. It also covered countries that knowingly purchased Russian oil or gas 30 days after the law's enactment, as well as those among the top five countries helping Russia evade sanctions.Also Read | The return of Middle East oil: Has Iran lost control of Strait of Hormuz & why are crude prices still up? Trump announced the waiver just days before several provisions of the legislation were due to take effect. He had signed the bill into law in mid-September.“I am hereby waiving the application of such sanctions, restrictions, and duties provided for in the Graham Act,” Trump said in an executive order issued on Friday evening.In the order, Trump said he had submitted a certification to Congress stating that granting the waiver at this stage was in the US national interest.The executive order comes as Trump has adopted a warmer stance towards Russia while publicly criticising Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy. He has even suggested that Ukraine needs a new leader.The proposed Russia sanctions had also raised concerns among countries that rely heavily on Russian oil imports. India, one of the largest buyers of Russian crude, was among the countries that expressed concerns about the legislation.Russia continues to be the single largest supplier of oil for India. A waiver of tariffs of up to 100% which may have come into place in the coming days means that India can continue importing oil in large numbers from Moscow without any economic fallout.If 100% tariffs had been imposed by the Trump administration, then it would have hit exporters as the US is the largest trading partner for India. At the same time, any sanctions may have rendered Russian crude economically unviable which would have added to the supply crunch at a time when Middle East tensions continue.Manoj Mishra, Partner and Tax Controversy Management Leader at Grant Thornton Bharat sees the waiver of the proposed 100% tariffs as a significant relief for India on both trade and energy security fronts.“Avoiding steep additional tariffs reduces the risk of disruption to energy sourcing amid ongoing tensions in the Middle East. Given that the US is India’s largest trading partner, the waiver also helps shield Indian exporters from potential adverse impacts across sectors,” he says.“Importantly, it eases a source of uncertainty in bilateral trade negotiations and creates a more conducive environment for advancing the India–US trade deal. However, businesses will continue to seek greater tariff clarity and predictability to support long-term export planning and supply-chain decisions,” he adds.The Middle East is a big supplier of energy needs for India - crude oil, LPG and LNG. Shipments through the Strait of Hormuz have been hit, leading India to diversify its energy basket more aggressively.Russian oil has played a big role in India’s crude oil imports at this time, with numbers hitting record highs a few months ago.In fact, Russia gradually became India’s largest crude supplier since the start of Moscow’s war with Ukraine, when European sanctions prompted Russia to sell oil to India and China at deep discounts.Last year, Donald Trump imposed 25% penal tariffs on India for its crude oil purchases from Russia, taking the total tariff figure to 50%. India did not stop buying crude from Russia, but after the US imposed sanctions on two Russian oil majors, the imports started coming down.In February this year, announcing while lowering tariffs on India to 18% and removing the 25% penal tariffs, Trump claimed that India would stop buying oil from Russia. India never made any such statement, and before a clear trend on its crude purchases from Russia could emerge, the Middle East conflict erupted.In between, the US waived sanctions on Russian crude to lower global crude oil prices, but even with those waivers lapsing, India continued to procure from Russia to meet its energy needs.The Trump administration’s move to sign the sanctions bill last month was also hinted to have been weighing on the India-US trade deal talks. With sanctions now being waived off, some movement may also be seen on that front, especially with Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal recently hinting that a draft is almost ready.But even as the threat of tariffs related to Russian oil recedes, India may still have to compete aggressively with China for crude from Moscow.Indian refiners expect Russian crude supplies to become even tighter in October and November as exports decline and competition from China intensifies, reports suggest.Also Read | Beijing’s billion-barrel weapon: Why India must prepare for China-driven oil prices The shortfall is likely to push the world's third-largest crude importer towards more expensive alternatives for the remainder of the year.In recent months, China, the world's largest crude importer, has increased its purchases as the Iran war disrupted supplies from the Middle East."Demand from China has been really high. They were willing to book cargoes in advance and to pay firmer prices compared to Indian refiners," a source involved in the sale of Russian crude told Reuters recently.Though Kpler data from October suggests that oil supplies are recovering and for now are averaging above 2 million barrels per day.
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump has waived sanctions, restrictions and duties provided for under the Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act. Trump announced the waiver just days before several provisions of the legislation were due to take effect. The legislation provided for tariffs of up to 100% within 30 days on goods entering the US from the five largest importers of Russian crude oil or gas.

Article Title: Man skipped filing ITR and got tax notice so he declared Rs 12.9 lakh income; department imposed 200% penalty of Rs 3.99 lakh on taxable amount, but ITAT cancels it
Article Text:
If a taxpayer is not told which specific legal provision forms the basis of the proposed penalty, the subsequent penalty proceedings are vitiated. (Image for representative purpose only)

What the case is about

Why did taxpayer win the case?

G.R. Infraprojects Limited vs. ACIT

When is penalty under Section 270A imposed?

You don’t file your income tax return (ITR) and declare your income only when the Income Tax Department sends you a notice. You face a 200% penalty but the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT) gives you relief on a technical ground.This is the case of a man in Jaipur who faced the situation, but got relief due to an error from the Income Tax Department. Let’s take a look:The man in this case failed to file his income tax return, and the Income Tax Department issued him a notice. He subsequently responded by filing an ITR for assessment year (AY) 2018-19, reporting an income of Rs 12.9 lakh.However, the Income Tax Assessing Officer (AO) took the view that this income would have remained outside the tax net had the department not issued the notice to the man. With this view, the AO, therefore, initiated penalty proceedings under Section 270A of the Income Tax Act.Also Read | She received Rs 9.04 lakh leave encashment on retiring from LIC; taxman allowed only Rs 3 lakh exemption, but ITAT Jaipur grants relief even after 1,277-day appeal delay What this provision does is it allows a penalty of up to 200% of the tax that is payable in cases which involve misreporting of income. In this case, the tax payable on the unreported income of Rs 12.9 lakh worked out to be around Rs 1.99 lakh. The AO consequently imposed the full 200% penalty of Rs 3.99 lakh.The Commissioner of Appeals (CIT(A)) also upheld the penalty, prompting the man to approach ITAT in Jaipur.On September 23, 2026, the ITAT Jaipur ruled in the man’s favour and set aside the penalty.Pranshu G, Partner at Ashok Pranshu & Co, told ET that the key issue was the AO's decision to impose the higher, 200% penalty for misreporting without specifying which particular clause of Section 270A(9) the man had allegedly violated.The ITAT found that neither the assessment order nor the penalty notice contained the necessary satisfaction identifying the alleged offence. As a result, the man had not been informed of the precise charge he was expected to contest.Also Read | She bought shares for Rs 13.5 lakh and sold them for Rs 77.47 lakh after 18 months; taxman denied capital gains exemption, but ITAT gives relief and deletes Rs 79 lakh in additions On examining the penalty notice issued to the man, ITAT Jaipur found that the document did not mention which specific limb of Section 270A(9) was being invoked to penalise him.The tribunal also pointed out the same deficiency in the assessment order. It said: “Similarly, when we see the assessment order, again proper satisfaction has not been recorded by the Assessing Officer as to under which part of Section 270A(9), the Act stood violated.”The ITAT observed that the law is well settled on this point. If a taxpayer is not told which specific legal provision forms the basis of the proposed penalty, the subsequent penalty proceedings are vitiated.To support its conclusion, the tribunal referred to the Rajasthan High Court's ruling in, D.B Civil Writ Petition No. 5594/2023, decided on January 2, 2024.An important additional point in the order is that the man’s declared income was accepted in the assessment without any addition or variation. The judgment also records that no revenue loss accrued to the department.The man had raised the absence of any addition or variation as a ground of appeal. However, the tribunal's stated basis for quashing the penalty was the failure to record the required satisfaction and specify the relevant provision of Section 270A(9).After considering the facts and the judicial precedents, the ITAT Jaipur concluded that the AO had failed to record the necessary satisfaction in the assessment order about which limb of Section 270A applied to the case. The AO had also omitted to specify the relevant part of Section 270A(9) in the notice issued under Section 274 read with Section 270A.The tribunal held that these omissions undermined the validity of the entire penalty proceedings. Consequently, the penalty imposed by the AO and subsequently upheld by the CIT(A) could not be sustained. The ITAT Jaipur therefore quashed the penalty.Also Read | Woman applied for 130 IPO shares, bank entered only 65; consumer commission awards Rs 37,000 for deficient service but rejects her Rs 40 lakh compensation claim Pranshu explains that Section 270A distinguishes between under-reporting of income and the more serious offence of misreporting. In ordinary cases of under-reported income, the penalty is 50% of the tax payable on the amount under-reported.The higher penalty of 200% applies only when the under-reporting arises from specific forms of misreporting listed under Section 270A(9). These include suppressing or misrepresenting facts, failing to record investments or receipts, making false entries in books of account, claiming expenditure without supporting evidence, and not reporting certain specified transactions.The detection of additional income, or a taxpayer's decision to offer such income for taxation, does not by itself automatically attract the 200% penalty.Pranshu says: "The Assessing Officer must establish misreporting and clearly identify the specific statutory limb invoked. This distinction is significant because Section 270A also excludes certain bona fide explanations and specified estimation-related situations from under-reported income."Also Read | Rs 5.89 crore FD interest slashed from 7.75% to 3.5% without notice; Delhi High Court rejects bank’s non-renewal argument and orders interest at an average of earlier rates
Article Summary: A man in Jaipur faced the situation, but got relief due to an error from the Income Tax Department. The key issue was the AO's decision to impose the higher, 200% penalty for misreporting without specifying which particular clause of Section 270A(9) the man had allegedly violated. The ITAT found that neither the assessment order nor the penalty notice contained the necessary satisfaction identifying the alleged offence.

Article Title: McClellan Air Force Base closed in 2001; 25 years later, the 3,000-acre Sacramento site has drawn about $600 million in investment, with 10 million sq ft of buildings and a public-use airport
Article Text:
Peacekeeper Gate at McClellan Air Force Base in 1995 (Image Credit: Wikipedia)

From military installation to commercial centre

$600 million investment and millions of square feet

A military airport becomes a public-use facility

Environmental cleanup remains part of the transformation

When McClellan Air Force Base closed in July 2001, the decision threatened thousands of jobs and raised concerns about the economic future of the surrounding Sacramento community. A quarter-century later, the former military installation has become McClellan Park, a business and industrial hub with around $600 million in investment, 10 million square feet of buildings and a public-use airport. According to the U.S. Air Force Civil Engineer Center (AFCEC), the redevelopment has involved partnerships between the Air Force, Sacramento County and private developers, alongside environmental restoration. A 2020 McClellan Park fact sheet documents the scale of investment and the site's transformation into a centre for businesses, transport and community services.McClellan Air Force Base was once one of the Sacramento region's major employers. The base supported military logistics and maintenance operations for more than six decades, employing thousands of military and civilian workers. Its closure was announced in 1995 under the federal Base Realignment and Closure process.The decision was expected to cost the local economy thousands of jobs and disrupt businesses that depended on the installation. Before the base officially closed, private businesses were brought into vacant buildings through a process known as a “hot transfer”. This helped retain some employment and allowed redevelopment to begin before the closure, according to McClellan Park’s historical account.The scale of the redevelopment is reflected in the site's infrastructure and commercial activity. McClellan Park's 2020 fact sheet records approximately $600 million in total economic investment, 10 million square feet of buildings and an occupancy rate of 90%. The site accommodates a mix of private businesses, government agencies, industrial facilities, offices and community organisations. Its large buildings have been adapted for different uses, allowing existing structures to serve new commercial purposes instead of requiring every business to start with new construction.The park's development potential also extends beyond its existing buildings. The 2020 fact sheet identifies another five million square feet of potential development, indicating that the property still had room to expand. The same document estimates that the site attracts between 15,000 and 17,000 daily visitors. These figures illustrate how a former military installation has become a major employment and business destination for the surrounding region.One of the most significant changes has been the conversion of the former military airport into a public-use airport serving general aviation. According to McClellan Park's fact sheet, the airport has a 10,600-foot runway. The property also contains seven miles of on-site railway connected directly to Union Pacific and BNSF rail lines, providing transport infrastructure alongside its commercial and industrial facilities.Former military buildings have found new purposes, too. The Air Force officers' club became The Officer's Club restaurant, while the former fitness centre now houses California Family Fitness. A former bowling alley has been converted into a classroom and learning centre operated by Gateway Community Charters. These adaptations demonstrate how existing facilities can support civilian businesses, education, recreation and public services after a military installation closes.The redevelopment has required more than attracting businesses and renovating buildings. Past military operations, waste disposal and chemical spills left soil and groundwater contamination that needed to be addressed.The Air Force has continued environmental restoration alongside the property's transition to civilian use. In 2007, the Air Force and Sacramento County established an agreement designed to accelerate cleanup and allow land to be transferred for redevelopment sooner. The arrangement brought together government agencies, environmental regulators and the private developer. The Air Force Civil Engineer Center reported in 2018 that McClellan's restoration programme had involved 325 sites requiring investigation. Cleanup measures included groundwater treatment, soil remediation and protective caps over contaminated areas. The project also received a US Environmental Protection Agency award recognising efforts to restore former federal facilities for productive reuse.McClellan Park's transformation illustrates how a closed military base can become a long-term economic asset when redevelopment, infrastructure investment and environmental restoration proceed together. Twenty-five years after the base shut down, the Sacramento site continues to serve businesses and the public while demonstrating a different future for land once dedicated to military operations.
Article Summary: McClellan Air Force Base was once one of the Sacramento region's major employers. The base supported military logistics and maintenance operations for more than six decades. Its closure was announced in 1995 under the federal Base Realignment and Closure process. A 2020 McClellan Park fact sheet documents the scale of investment and the site's transformation.

Article Title: Is there govt scheme to help pregnant minor rape survivors become self-reliant?: Bombay HC to Maharashtra govt
Article Text:
Bombay HC





MUMBAI: Bombay High Court has asked state govt whether it has a scheme to assist girls who are survivors of sexual assault and are required to undergo medical termination of pregnancy to become self-reliant.“In our view, financial assistance alone may not provide a sustainable solution in the long run. However, if such a girl is imparted appropriate skills or is enabled to pursue her education, she may become self-reliant and would not have to depend upon financial assistance granted by this court,” said Justices Bharati Dangre and Ashish Chavan on Monday.On Oct 9, they allowed MTP of the 28-week pregnancy of a 15-year-old sexual assault survivor and directed the petition to be tagged with two other petitions where two teenaged survivors were allowed to terminate their 25-week pregnancies. In a few matters, HC had indicated to the state to suggest some “methodology” by which such survivors “are assisted in any manner”.State’s advocate M P Thakur submitted a Govt Resolution (GR) issued by the women and child development department that set out a scheme under the Juvenile Justice Act and its rules.The judges noted the GR covers “various categories of children who are victims of offences” under the POCSO Act but “does not specifically identify this category…”“A girl who is a victim of an offence under the POCSO Act falls in a completely different category,” the bench said.“It is not necessary that, in every such case, she must be admitted to an institution or an observation home. Rather, the focus should be on enabling her to overcome the trauma with the assistance of her family members, while simultaneously making arrangements for her future so that she can become self-reliant and secure a means of livelihood. ”The judges said they “expect” Thakur to obtain instructions whether women and child development or social welfare departments have formulated any scheme “for the benefit of girls falling in this category”.The judges also asked to check with the women and child development commissioner whether there exists any scheme “specifically” for survivors of offences under POCSO Act, “apart from Manodhairya scheme, or whether any other scheme which provides financial assistance to such victims”.
Article Summary: Bombay High Court asked state govt whether it has a scheme to assist girls who are survivors of sexual assault. Justices Bharati Dangre and Ashish Chavan said financial assistance alone may not provide a sustainable solution in the long run. They allowed MTP of the 28-week pregnancy of a 15-year-old sexual assault survivor.

Article Title: India-US trade deal: First phase finalised, legal drafting under way, says Piyush Goyal
Article Text:
India-US trade deal

The much-awaited India-US trade deal has cleared its first phase and moved to the legal drafting stage, commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal said on Thursday.He said that the pact would be operationalised once India gains a competitive advantage over its peer countries. The minister further expressed hope that the process would be completed soon."US bilateral trade agreement's first tranche has been finalised and it is going through final contours, the legal drafting and we hope to be able to finalise that soon and operationalise that once we get the competitive advantage over our peer countries," Goyal said.The minister also provided an update on India's trade negotiations with the European Union, saying that the free trade agreement would be signed in December and is expected to take effect in February or March next year.Earlier in the day, US Ambassador to India Sergio Gor also said that the two nations have cleared the major items on their trade deal checklist. Gor described the pace of negotiations as “incredible.”Gor also spoke about the US legislation that could pave the way for sanctions on countries purchasing Russian oil and gas or helping others evade sanctions. He said US President Donald Trump was expected to decide on the matter within the next 10 days.The legislation received 86 votes in the 100-member US Senate and gives the President the authority to impose sanctions on countries involved in buying Russian oil and gas or facilitating sanctions evasion. Gor said the provisions were not aimed at any particular country, including India.“...We have ongoing discussions on that as it passed with overwhelming bipartisan support. That law got 86 votes out of 100 in our Senate... These sanctions options that Congress passed, they are not targeted at any individual country. It is three different buckets; one is oil, the second is gas, the third is sanctions evasion.”Explaining how countries could fall within the scope of the measures, Gor said their inclusion was based on numbers. He added that India was among several countries that fell into one of the categories, but said the intention was to end the war rather than punish any country.“It just happens that India does fall in one of those buckets, along with a lot of other countries. The goal is not to punish anyone. The goal is to try to bring an end to this war. I do think the president will make a determination on that over the next few days.”Gor said India offered significant opportunities for American businesses, citing the size of its market and the government's approach to foreign investment.India and the US have been negotiating a proposed bilateral trade agreement since early 2025, seeking to address tariff-related tensions, remove non-tariff barriers and improve market access. India is also pushing for more favourable tariff terms for its exports to the US than those available to competing economies.
Article Summary: The much-awaited India-US trade deal has cleared its first phase and moved to the legal drafting stage, commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal said. He said that the pact would be operationalised once India gains a competitive advantage over its peer countries. Goyal also provided an update on India's trade negotiations with the European Union, saying that the free trade agreement would be signed in December and is expected to take effect in February or March next year.

Article Title: Direct tax mop-up rises 13.21% to Rs 13.38 lakh crore till October 14
Article Text:
Net direct tax collections rise 13.21% to Rs 13.38 lakh crore

NEW DELHI: India's net direct tax mop-up reached Rs 13,37,866.98 crore in FY2026-27 as of October 14, marking a 13.21 per cent increase from Rs 11,81,786.98 crore collected during the same period last year, data released by the income tax department showed.The increase came alongside a rise in gross collections, which climbed to Rs 16,03,066.12 crore from Rs 13,95,278.39 crore in the year-ago period. However, the amount returned to taxpayers also increased, with refunds rising 24.22 per cent year-on-year to Rs 2,65,199.14 crore from Rs 2,13,491.41 crore.Net corporate tax receipts stood at Rs 5,99,062.48 crore as of October 14, compared with Rs 4,96,798.62 crore in the corresponding period of the previous financial year.Gross corporate tax collections rose to Rs 7,52,961.56 crore from Rs 6,43,721.45 crore. Refunds issued against corporate tax increased to Rs 1,53,899.08 crore, up from Rs 1,46,922.83 crore in the same period last year.Net non-corporate tax collections increased to Rs 6,91,965.71 crore from Rs 6,53,804.16 crore a year earlier. This category includes taxes paid by individuals, Hindu Undivided Families, firms and other entities.Gross collections under the non-corporate tax category rose to Rs 8,03,245.26 crore, compared with Rs 7,20,353.91 crore in the corresponding period of the previous financial year.Refunds in this category registered a more pronounced increase, reaching Rs 1,11,279.55 crore against Rs 66,549.75 crore a year earlier.Collections from the Securities Transaction Tax (STT) rose to Rs 46,840.43 crore as of October 14, compared with Rs 30,901.81 crore in the corresponding period last year. The increase reflected higher collections from transactions in securities.The overall figures show that the rise in gross direct tax receipts was accompanied by a faster increase in refunds. While gross collections grew 14.89 per cent year-on-year, refunds increased 24.22 per cent, bringing the growth in net direct tax collections to 13.21 per cent.The data covers collections up to October 14 and provides a snapshot of direct tax receipts during the first half of the current financial year.
Article Summary: India's net direct tax mop-up reached Rs 13,37,866.98 crore in FY2026-27 as of October 14. This is a 13.21 per cent increase from Rs 11,81,786.98 collected during the same period last year. Refunds issued against corporate tax increased to Rs 1,53,899.08 crore.

Article Title: Kospi hits the brakes: South Korean benchmark plunges 7.5%, triggers 'sidecar' stop for investors
Article Text:
Kospi tumbles over 7% as tech stocks lose steam

Samsung, SK Hynix lead South Korean market rout

‘Sidecar’ triggered

South Korea’s stock market hit a rough patch on Thursday, with the benchmark Kospi plunging 7.49% as technology stocks came under heavy selling pressure. The rout spread across Asian markets, prompting the country’s exchange operator to trigger a five-minute trading halt on programme sell orders after a sharp drop in index futures.The KOSPI dropped 450.02 points to 5,558.79, putting it on course for a seventh consecutive session of losses, its longest losing streak since September 2024. The index has fallen nearly 35% from its record high in June.The pressure on Asian equities followed a technology-led sell-off on Wall Street after US consumer price inflation accelerated more than expected in September. The data fuelled concerns that the Federal Reserve could raise interest rates later this year, putting technology companies and AI-related stocks under further pressure.MSCI’s broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan fell 3.3%, while Japan’s Nikkei 225 declined 4.8%. S&P 500 e-mini futures were down 0.5%.Major technology companies accounted for some of the steepest losses on the South Korean exchange. Samsung Electronics shares fell 9.05%, while SK Hynix dropped 11.06%, reflecting the broader weakness across Asia’s semiconductor supply chain.Battery maker LG Energy Solution lost 3.44%. Hyundai Motor declined 3.99%, while sister automaker Kia Corp fell 2.03%.The selling extended to other Asian technology companies. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) fell 2%, while Japan’s memory chipmaker Kioxia Holdings plunged more than 11%. SoftBank Group, an investor in AI, declined 9.4%.Market breadth in South Korea remained heavily negative. Of the 889 stocks traded, 768 declined and 90 advanced. Foreign investors sold shares worth a net 355.6 billion won.The won, meanwhile, strengthened 0.21% to 1,339.5 per dollar on the onshore settlement platform, compared with its previous close of 1,342.3.The sharp decline prompted the South Korean exchange operator to activate a sell-side “sidecar”, an automatic mechanism designed to temporarily cool trading during periods of heavy selling. The measure suspends program sell orders for five minutes after steep losses in index futures.The trigger came as the KOSPI extended its decline to seven consecutive sessions. The benchmark has now shed nearly 35% since its June record, with retail investors among those hit hardest during a sell-off in July, when the index fell around 20%. Losses in highly leveraged single-stock exchange-traded funds (ETFs) contributed to the damage during that period.The sell-off in Asia followed Wall Street’s third consecutive session of losses. The S&P 500 declined 1.1% overnight, while the Nasdaq Composite fell 1.9%. A gauge of semiconductor stocks recorded its sixth straight day of losses as investors reassessed the outlook for companies sensitive to borrowing costs.Meanwhile, in South Korea’s bond market, December futures on three-year treasury bonds rose 0.12 point to 103.00. The yield on the most liquid three-year Korean treasury bond fell 3 basis points to 3.855%, while the benchmark 10-year yield declined 2.1 basis points to 4.224%.Oil prices also moved lower, with Brent crude falling 1.7% to $104.20 a barrel. Traders weighed the potential impact of US sanctions relief on oil supply against attacks on shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.
Article Summary: Kospi plunges 7.49% as technology stocks come under heavy selling pressure. The country’s exchange operator triggered a five-minute trading halt on programme sell orders after a sharp drop in index futures. The pressure on Asian equities followed a technology-led sell-off on Wall Street after US consumer price inflation accelerated.

Article Title: Heavy rain lashes Delhi-NCR, IMD issues orange alert
Article Text:
Heavy rain and thunderstorms impacted multiple areas of Delhi-NCR on Thursday

(With Agency Inputs)





NEW DELHI: Heavy rain lashed several parts of Delhi-NCR on Thursday, with thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds sweeping across the region.The India Meteorological Department (IMD) issued an orange alert for the national capital.The weather department forecast rainfall of 5-15 mm per hour, accompanied by thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds blowing at 40-60 kmph.The alert remained in force until 2 pm, with intermittent spells of rain expected in several parts of Delhi, the IMD said.The minimum temperature in the city settled at 23.3 degrees Celsius, 3.7 degrees above normal. The maximum temperature is expected to hover around 29 degrees Celsius, bringing down daytime temperatures, it said.Experts attributed the sudden spell of rain to a western disturbance and a cyclonic circulation over adjoining areas.They said the conditions were part of a normal post-monsoon weather pattern, with Delhi and other parts of the region likely to receive intermittent showers.
Article Summary: The India Meteorological Department (IMD) issued an orange alert for the national capital. Rainfall of 5-15 mm per hour, accompanied by thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds. Minimum temperature in the city settled at 23.3 degrees Celsius, 3.7 degrees above normal.

Article Title: CBI arrests SFIO deputy director, advocate in Rs 1 crore bribe case linked to DHFL scam probe
Article Text:
The CBI arrested Harish Kumar Tanwar, an Indian Revenue Service (IRS) officer of the 2017 batch. (Representative image)





CHENNAI: The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) has arrested a deputy director-level officer of the Serious Fraud Investigation Office (SFIO), Ministry of Corporate Affairs, posted in Chennai, a Delhi-based advocate and the advocate’s relative for allegedly demanding a Rs 1 crore bribe to favour a complainant in an investigation into the DHFL scam.The CBI arrested Harish Kumar Tanwar, an Indian Revenue Service (IRS) officer of the 2017 batch who is currently posted as deputy director of the SFIO in Chennai, advocate Bharat Sharma of New Delhi, and Aryan Sharma, a relative of the advocate, after laying a trap. The arrests followed the advocate’s alleged receipt of Rs 20 lakh from the complainant as part payment of the demanded bribe on behalf of the SFIO officer.According to the CBI, the case was registered against Tanwar, the advocate and others following allegations that they had demanded Rs 1 crore from the complainant to allegedly favour him in an investigation into the DHFL scam being conducted by the SFIO.The CBI verified the complaint before registering the case on Tuesday. It subsequently laid a trap and arrested the three accused after the advocate allegedly received Rs 20 lakh from the complainant on behalf of the SFIO officer.The CBI also conducted searches at the premises of the public servant and the advocate and recovered incriminating material related to the case.The case has been registered under Section 61(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, relating to criminal conspiracy, and Sections 7 and 7A of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988.
Article Summary: The CBI arrested Harish Kumar Tanwar, an Indian Revenue Service (IRS) officer of the 2017 batch. Tanwar is currently posted as deputy director of the SFIO in Chennai. The CBI laid a trap after the advocate allegedly received Rs 20 lakh from the complainant.

Article Title: Elon Musk's 'China prediction' may add to the pain of 20 of the most valuable global technology companies across US and Europe that have lost over $1 trillion dollars in less than 5 days
Article Text:
Elon Musk's 'China prediction' may add to the pain of 20 of the most valuable global technology companies across US and Europe that have lost over $1 trillion dollars in less than 5 days

Here's how much Nvidia , AMD, Micron and other companies lost

Why AI and semiconductor stocks are selling off

A sell-off in artificial intelligence (AI) and semiconductor shares has wiped out more than $1 trillion in market value from 20 of the world’s most valuable technology companies in less than five days, a report has said. It attributes this to a combination of interest rate hikes, increasing AI infrastructure costs and intensifying competition. Adding to the anxiety, Chinese chipmaker ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT) announced plans to accelerate its memory chip manufacturing capabilities, putting fresh pressure on an already rattled global market. Elon Musk reacted to the news saying that China will be making “a LOT of RAM in 2028”, a view that could add to that pressure.The billionaire’s commentary arrives as investors grapple with growing anxiety over an impending global memory chip oversupply as early as 2029, spurred by chipmakers worldwide aggressively building out production capacity to meet AI workloads. CXMT recently said that it achieved a major architectural breakthrough to boost memory density by packing more data into tighter spaces.US semiconductor giants and specialised cloud infrastructure providers continued to slide in premarket trading on Thursday (October 15) following a punishing Wednesday session on Wall Street.Nvidia fell 1.8%; Micron Technology dropped 4.4%; AMD slipped 3.5%; Oracle traded down 2%; Neocloud providers took sharp hits, with CoreWeave falling 5.3% and Nebius retreating 4%.Notably, the rout was not confined to US exchanges, deepening across major trading hubs in Asia and Europe. South Korean memory chip giant SK Hynix plummeted more than 10%, while rival Samsung Electronics dropped 8.73%. Related tech and component suppliers saw steep declines as well, with LG Innotek sinking 8.95%, Seoul Semiconductor sliding 9.28%, and Samsung SDI down 6.26%.In Japan, technology investment firm SoftBank Group tumbled 7.9%. Testing equipment supplier Advantest plunged nearly 14%, Tokyo Electron lost 6.45%, and Renesas Electronics fell 8%. Similarly, in Taiwan, leading contract foundry TSMC slipped 1.81%. When it comes to Europe, advanced lithography supplier ASML traded down 6.6%, ASM International sank 9.6%, Germany’s Infineon Technologies lost 9.4%, and Nokia dropped 5%.Market analysts and investors point to a convergence of macroeconomic headwinds, financing bottlenecks, and long-term supply threats that are eroding sentiment across the sector. Inflation has raised concerns that elevated interest rates will increase the cost of capital needed to finance massive data center and AI infrastructure deployments.Top industry leaders have voiced caution regarding capital access. On Monday, the chief executives of Broadcom and Intel warned that financing could soon become the primary headwind facing the AI boom.
Article Summary: 20 of the world's most valuable technology companies have lost over $1 trillion dollars in less than 5 days. The rout was not confined to US exchanges, deepening across major trading hubs in Asia and Europe. South Korean memory chip giant SK Hynix plummeted more than 10%, while rival Samsung Electronics dropped 8.73%.

Article Title: 56 year old Chestnut trees, said to be one of America’s last remaining Chestnut Groves, at risk of being wiped out by datacenter labelled as: 'One of the largest single AI infrastructure investments i
Article Text:
Why the West Virginia chestnut grove matters

What is the Monarch Compute Campus

A conflict between AI infrastructure and conservation

In 1904, a necrotrophic fungus called chestnut blight began devastating North America's native chestnut trees. This fungus, brought across the Pacific on chestnut trees from Japan and China, attacks tree bark and kills the above-ground portions of susceptible trees. The disease eventually wiped out billions of chestnut trees across the US. More than a century later, a grove of approximately 200 blight-resistant American chestnut trees in West Virginia is facing the threat of being cleared to make way for a large-scale artificial intelligence data center.Planted in the 1970s, the 56-year-old trees are a valuable source of genetic material that could help restore the species. However, the proposed Monarch Compute Campus, developed by Nscale in collaboration with Nvidia and Caterpillar, could put the grove at risk. The project is planned to span more than 2,250 acres and provide 8 gigawatts of computing capacity, with its developer calling it “one of the largest single AI infrastructure investments in US history. ”The chestnut blight outbreak destroyed an estimated 4 billion American chestnut trees across the US.Although surviving stumps can produce new shoots, these often succumb to the disease before reaching maturity.Researchers and horticulturists have since worked to preserve the species through breeding programmes and blight-resistant hybrids. However, mature chestnut groves remain uncommon. According to the supplied report, fewer than 4,300 acres of fruit-producing chestnut trees existed across the continental US in 2023.The grove contains about 200 blight-resistant chestnut trees planted in the 1970s from surviving wild American chestnuts. Their age and genetic material make them a potentially important resource for future restoration efforts.A report published in From the Front Lines: Struggles for Justice by the New York-based Global Justice Ecology Project has raised concerns about the grove's future.“Planted in the 1970s from wild surviving American chestnuts, this orchard is a vital ‘genetics library,'” the publication explains, describing it as “the primary seed source to restore the species across West Virginia.”The trees could provide seeds and genetic material for efforts to establish new chestnut populations. Losing the grove could therefore affect more than the existing trees, potentially reducing the resources available to future restoration projects.The proposed data center development is being built by Nscale in collaboration with Nvidia and Caterpillar. Under the current plans, the completed campus will cover more than 2,250 acres and provide 8 gigawatts of computing capacity for AI companies, including Anthropic.The development represents a substantial investment in computing infrastructure as technology companies expand their capacity to train and run artificial intelligence models.Nscale has described the project as “one of the largest single AI infrastructure investments in US history, anchoring America’s compute foundation.”The scale of the planned facility could make protecting the grove difficult, especially if the trees fall within areas designated for construction.The potential loss of the chestnut grove highlights a conflict between expanding AI infrastructure and preserving biological resources. Data centers require large sites, electricity and supporting infrastructure, while conservation projects depend on protecting habitats and maintaining genetic diversity.According to From the Front Lines, the surviving chestnut trees are “irreplaceable” because they could support future restoration work.The grove's future will depend on the development plans and whether its preservation can be reconciled with construction. For conservationists, protecting these trees could help retain an important source of genetic material for restoring American chestnuts to their former range.
Article Summary: A grove of 200 blight-resistant American chestnut trees in West Virginia is facing the threat of being cleared to make way for a large-scale artificial intelligence data center. The 56-year-old trees are a valuable source of genetic material that could help restore the species. The proposed Monarch Compute Campus, developed by Nscale in collaboration with Nvidia and Caterpillar, could put the grove at risk.

Article Title: Microsoft president Brad Smith breaks silence on the US government suspending Microsoft from Green Card sponsorship programme; says: We should all be worried about ...
Article Text:
In pic: Microsoft president Brad Smith

What Microsoft president Brad Smith said

Microsoft president Brad Smith rejects visa fraud accusations against the company

Microsoft president Brad Smith has warned that the US government’s move suspending Microsoft and other tech giants from the Green Card sponsorship programme could hurt the country’s ‌technological competitiveness and drive talent overseas. In an exclusive interview with Decoded by Politico, Brad Smith pushed back against Vice President JD Vance's accusations that Microsoft had abused the H-1B visa ⁠program, calling them "completely off base". He also pointed at the irony that the White House put restrictions on Microsoft on the same day it gave a medal to Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella, a former H-1B skilled visa holder from India.Expressing concerns about the impact the crackdown on the ability of the U.S. to attract top tech talent, Smith said: “I think we should all be worried about sending — intentionally or inadvertently or otherwise — signals that send the most talented next wave of AI [or] SI software engineers to other countries, rather than the United States”. Notably, Brad Smith’s comments come almost a week after the US government announced that it will bar Microsoft, TCS, Infosys and other companies from seeking green cards for skilled foreign ​workers.During the interview, Microsoft president Brad Smith said: “We should consider the fact that when the president honored six Americans with these technology and science medals, five of the six had come to the United States as immigrants,” adding “And those five individuals, if you put them and their companies together, have companies that have a market value equal to more than 25% of the market value of the total S&P 500. ”“Think about what those five individuals have done for the well-being, even the wealth and standard of living, of Americans across the country. Let’s not put that at risk,” he continued.Brad Smith also rejected JD Vance’s visa fraud accusations and called the vice president’s claims “completely off base.” He said someone “had failed to inform the vice president accurately about our numbers,” noting that the “vast majority” of Microsoft’s green card applications were for long-time employees, not new hires.“Unfortunately, it’s just because the green card backlog is so long,” said Smith.Denying that the company pays foreign-born workers less, the Microsoft executive said “it doesn’t matter whether you came on a visa or you’re an American worker, everybody has the same compensation system.” And he complained that the more than 9,000 U.S.-born workers that Microsoft hired last year were “left out of the narrative” propagated by the White House.“We will stand by our record,” said Smith. “And I hope that folks at the White House might look again and look at what we think is a more accurate picture.”
Article Summary: Microsoft president Brad Smith has warned that the US government’s move suspending Microsoft and other tech giants from the Green Card sponsorship programme could hurt the country's technological competitiveness. Brad Smith pushed back against Vice President JD Vance's accusations that Microsoft had abused the H-1B visa program.

Article Title: Jeff Bezos’ has invested billions of his fortune into SpaceX rival Blue Origin; documents reveal extraordinary commitment; what Amazon founder said on winners in the space
Article Text:
Jeff Bezos’s $2 billion is part of Blue Origin’s first-ever capital raise

Revenue targets jump from $800 million to $30 billion

Leaner operations under Limp

New Glenn and the SpaceX challenge

What Bezos said about winners

Amazon founder Jeff Bezos has invested a staggering $30 billion of his personal fortune into rocket company Blue Origin since founding it in 2000, including a fresh $2 billion commitment as the company ramps up efforts to challenge SpaceX's dominance in the commercial space industry, according to a Wall Street Journal report. Documents reviewed by the publication reveal the scale of the Amazon founder's financial backing for Blue Origin, underscoring a long-term commitment that has helped transform the company into a major space player with around 15,000 employees and ambitious growth plans.The latest $2 billion commitment from Bezos forms part of Blue Origin's first-ever fundraising round involving external investors. The company has already secured $10 billion in the oversubscribed financing round, which values the company at approximately $140 billion, according to the report. Bezos, whose net worth stood at about $275 billion in late September according to the Bloomberg Billionaires Index, has previously sold Amazon shares to help fund Blue Origin's expansion.The company is betting heavily on future growth across rocket launches, satellite communications and artificial intelligence infrastructure. Blue Origin generated about $800 million in revenue in 2025, according to the documents cited by the Journal.The company expects revenue to grow to roughly $1.4 billion this year before surging to more than $30 billion by 2030. Part of that projected growth is expected to come from a satellite communications business that has yet to launch hardware into orbit, as well as a planned fleet of AI-focused satellites. Rocket launch services are also expected to contribute significantly to future revenue.The company has been sharpening its operations. It carried out a major layoff last year and stopped suborbital tourism flights. Chief Executive Dave Limp, who took the job almost three years ago, has emphasized accelerating missions and technical development, and the company is eager to deliver for customers such as NASA.Blue Origin faces competition across its business lines from other rocket operators and satellite and spacecraft companies, but especially from industry leader SpaceX. According to the documents, Blue Origin expects to narrow SpaceX’s lead with its New Glenn vehicles.New Glenn is a massive rocket with a reusable booster. Blue Origin has flown it on three missions, but it has not flown since a vehicle exploded on a Florida launchpad in May. The company is redeveloping that complex.Bezos said in an interview last year that the space industry has plenty of room for winners. “SpaceX is going to be successful. Blue Origin is going to be successful. And there’s some company out there right now that hasn’t even been founded yet that is also going to be successful,” he said.
Article Summary: Jeff Bezos' $2 billion is part of Blue Origin’s first-ever capital raise. Company expects revenue to grow to roughly $1.4 billion this year before surging to more than $30 billion by 2030. Blue Origin faces competition across its business lines from other rocket operators and satellite and spacecraft companies.

Article Title: As Apple becomes the first company to join Nvidia in $5 trillion club, here's the big 'iPhone message' from investors
Article Text:
The investor message: confidence despite cost pressure

Tim Cook’s record

AI remains the challenge

OpenAI threat and legal fight

Apple has become the second company after Nvidia to close with a market value above $5 trillion, underscoring investors’ continued faith in the iPhone maker despite the growing conversion over increasing hardware costs, AI competition and slowing growth. According to a report by Wall Street Journal, Apple ended trading a market capitalisation of about $5.005 trillion, making the first time the company has finished a trading session above the $5 trillion threshold. The milestone caps the tenure of former CEO Tim Cook, who oversaw a 13-fold increase in Apple’s market value during his 15 years at the helm. While, the rise of Nvidia has been fuelled by the AI boom and massive data centre sending, Apple’s ascent reflects something different: investor confidence in the resilience of its ecosystem and, most importantly, the willingness of iPhone users to continue paying more for Apple devices.Investors are so confident in Apple’s business that they have pushed up its shares even as big cost increases threaten profit margins. The cost of memory and storage chips inside iPhones, Macs and iPads has soared because data-center demand has caused shortages. Apple has responded by raising prices across its device lineup, including for older iPhone models that would typically get a price cut.In theory, that could hurt Apple, since buyers might wait longer to upgrade.Yet Apple shares have jumped 25% since the first wave of price increases.Bank of America analyst Wamsi Mohan said investors believe Apple’s customers will pay the higher prices, letting the company earn as much or more in total profit even if margins fall. He added that the new foldable iPhone Duo is likely to be popular and that the new Siri AI should prompt upgrades.Cook’s act will be tough to follow. During his 15-year tenure as CEO, which ended Aug. 31, Apple’s market capitalization grew 13-fold. The company nearly quadrupled its annual iPhone sales. Its services business grew from $10 billion a year to more than $100 billion. The Apple Watch and AirPods, which he launched, together generate more than $30 billion a year. Apple also returned more than $1 trillion to shareholders through buybacks and dividends.Apple shares trade at a premium to the S&P 500 even though its revenue is growing more slowly than the index average. Analysts say that is because investors see the shares as safe and the business as predictable. A key to that has been limited capital spending, which boosts returns and lowers risk. That has been especially clear during the AI build-out, when big tech rivals have rushed to spend huge sums on data centers while Apple has stuck to making devices and selling high-margin services for them.AI has long been seen as Apple’s Achilles’ heel. The company failed to build its own frontier model and let Siri fall far behind rivals. Apple hopes the new Siri AI, built with Google’s help and released this fall, will change that. It still lags rival AI systems in key respects, but it is built directly into the iPhone, which many people already use. Apple also has access to more personal data, which could in theory power compelling features, though new AI agents show the technology is advancing faster than Apple can keep up.Perhaps the biggest threat is OpenAI, which is planning a family of AI-powered devices and has poached hundreds of Apple employees to drive its hardware strategy. Apple sued OpenAI in July, alleging it stole trade secrets. OpenAI has said it is “not aware of any evidence that this complaint has merit.” In a new filing Wednesday, it alleged that Apple poached one of its own employees, who took confidential files with him. Apple said it found no evidence supporting that allegation.AI could be where Ternus makes his mark, the Journal said. He could usher in a new era of innovation and growth, or Apple could finally lose its status as the company that defines how people interact with computers.
Article Summary: Investors are so confident in Apple’s business that they have pushed up its shares even as big cost increases threaten profit margins. Apple shares trade at a premium to the S&P 500 even though its revenue is growing more slowly than the index average. Investors see the shares as safe and the business as predictable.

Article Title: Justice Department cracks on America's 'North Korean employees problem'; says: More than 70 US companies affected, shares scammers email IDs
Article Text:
How the scheme worked

FBI raids laptop farms

Arrests and charges

Texas raids

Email IDs made public

Changing tactics

The US Department of Justice (DOJ) has announced a coordinated crackdown on a North Korean remote IT worker scheme that allegedly infiltrated dozens of American companies using stolen identities, warning businesses about a growing threat that generated millions of dollars for Pyongyang. More than 70 US companies were affected by the operation, according to the department. The action includes criminal charges against multiple suspects, two arrests, searches of dozens of suspected "laptop farms" and the seizure of approximately 187 laptops and related devices used to help North Korean operatives obtain remote jobs at US companies.According to an indictment unsealed in the Northern District of Ohio, North Korean workers got remote jobs at US companies from 2019 to around July 2025. They used stolen or fabricated identity documents, plus VPNs and proxy infrastructure, to appear to be U.S.-based employees.U.S.-based facilitators hosted the laptops that victim companies issued to these “employees” at their homes, the so-called laptop farms. They set up the machines, installed remote-access software and transferred the earnings to accounts controlled by North Korea.The scheme generated about $3 million in revenue, believed to have been sent to sanctioned North Korean entities.Victims included companies in health care, communications, cyber support, retail and manufacturing across Ohio, 16 other states and Washington, D.C.As part of the operation, the FBI executed searches at more than 40 locations in Texas believed to be connected to "laptop farms" used by North Korean workers. Investigators seized approximately 187 laptops and remote-access devices that allegedly enabled the fraud. The DOJ said the activity has been linked to a threat group known as "Famous Chollima," which has previously been associated with North Korean IT worker operationsTwo US nationals, Michael James Bostelle of Pennsylvania and Juan Cecilio Pena Carrillo of Texas, were arrested on charges of wire fraud, money laundering and identity theft. The indictment also names 10 China-based defendants, with two more under seal. The FBI said 14 people in total face charges.From Sept. 21 to Sept. 25, the FBI searched more than 40 residences in Texas in what it calls Operation Lonestar Roundup. Agents seized about 187 laptops and KVM devices. Cybersecurity firm CrowdStrike identified the group as “Famous Chollima.”“Every laptop farm we dismantle shuts down a revenue stream that the North Korean government relies on to fund weapons programs,” said U.S. Attorney Ryan Raybould of the Northern District of Texas.The department published 11 email addresses it says the operatives used and urged employers to add them to their screening indicators:Bright.star.me208@gmail.comMerrttank.bz@gmail.comrandyryang@gmail.commichaelb860102@gmail.comassassinki211@gmail.comdev.jerryyang@gmail.comdenis.turgenev2021@gmail.comyesiree.cano825@gmail.comthomasdenzelbrown@gmail.comanthonyortega4592@gmail.comtyler.j.palmi38@gmail.comThe FBI issued a public service announcement with guidance for companies. It warns that North Korean workers increasingly recruit American facilitators to get around better detection. They give those facilitators a wider range of tasks and sometimes subcontract whole jobs to third-party foreign nationals. Some have also committed data extortion and stolen sensitive company data.A 2022 advisory said individual North Korean IT workers can earn up to $300,000 a year. The State Department is offering rewards of up to $5 million for information that helps disrupt North Korea’s illicit financial activities.The department noted that the court filings contain allegations, and all defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty.
Article Summary: More than 70 US companies were affected by the operation, according to the department. The action includes criminal charges against multiple suspects, two arrests, searches of dozens of suspected "laptop farms" and the seizure of 187 laptops and related devices. The DOJ said the activity has been linked to a threat group known as "Famous Chollima"

Article Title: World’s most valuable memory chip maker to US: Accept this 'China condition' if you want us to build factories in America
Article Text:
Representative Image. Credit: SK Hynix

Why SK Hynix wants US approval for its China facility

"The installation of equipment for Mod B is being carried out in close consultation with and under authorisation from the US government."

"No capacity expansion is being sought for the Dalian Mod B, which was completed in 2023."

US export restrictions complicate SK Hynix’s plans

"Biden-era loophole."

SK Hynix’s plans for a US factory

NAND memory market drives expansion plans

SK Hynix is reportedly seeking US approval to expand its China operations. According to a report by the news agency Reuters, the South Korean memory chipmaker wants Washington’s permission to export additional US-made semiconductor manufacturing equipment to its Dalian facility in China. The report cited two people familiar with the matter, who said SK Hynix has made this a condition for funding its planned investment in American manufacturing.The report claims that the company’s US unit, Solidigm, is seeking an export licence to install equipment for producing NAND flash memory chips in unused space at the Chinese site. As per the report, the company is linking its plans for a new NAND factory in the US to its ability to increase production in China.The development comes as the Trump administration pushes foreign semiconductor companies to establish manufacturing facilities in America, while Washington continues to restrict China’s access to advanced chipmaking technology.Solidigm wants to install additional equipment at SK Hynix’s Dalian facility to manufacture NAND flash memory chips. These chips power solid-state drives (SSDs), which are increasingly important for data centres supporting artificial intelligence (AI) and cloud computing workloads.The Dalian facility already uses semiconductor manufacturing equipment supplied by US companies, including Lam Research, Applied Materials and KLA. However, Solidigm needs additional authorisation to purchase and install more US-made equipment at the site.The report cited one person familiar with the matter, who said the company believes increasing production in China would help Solidigm finance a NAND manufacturing facility in the US. It would also help pave the way for expanding production capacity in America.In a statement to Reuters, SK Hynix said,The company added,Solidigm declined to comment, while the US Department of Commerce did not respond to a request for comment.The request comes as Washington works to limit China’s access to semiconductor manufacturing technology. The US government has imposed export restrictions on chipmaking equipment to slow Beijing’s development of advanced semiconductors used in AI and military applications.Last year, the US Department of Commerce revoked authorisations that had allowed SK Hynix and Samsung to obtain US equipment for their Chinese factories without applying for individual licences. The department described the previous arrangements as aInstead, the government said it would issue export licences allowing the companies to operate their existing Chinese facilities, while signalling that it did not expect to approve applications for capacity expansion or technology upgrades.In December 2025, the department issued a licence for SK Hynix’s Dalian plant for 2026 but restricted the amount of equipment that could be exported. One source said the company has not yet been approved for more US-made equipment and technology for 2027.Mod B is a manufacturing facility in Dalian, built in 2023. Even after the memory market went into the doldrums, the equipment was not installed.The proposed American NAND factory is part of SK Hynix’s broader efforts to expand its manufacturing presence in the US. Reuters reported last month that Solidigm was considering building a NAND flash memory factory in the country.The company is also reportedly in talks with Intel to lease part of its planned chipmaking facility in Ohio. Separately, SK Hynix has broken ground on an advanced packaging plant in Indiana focused on high-bandwidth memory (HBM), which is used in AI systems.Building semiconductor fabrication plants, commonly called fabs, requires billions of dollars and can take several years. Another source said that Solidigm is also weighing an initial public offering (IPO) as early as next year, which could provide additional funding for its US factory plans.SK Hynix’s request comes after the NAND market has recovered from a previous downturn and struggled with supply constraints. Walt Coon, memory industry expert at TechInsights, said NAND pricing has surged sevenfold since mid-2023 and the market is likely to remain tight over the next few years.The company is one of the two leading global suppliers of NAND flash memory, alongside Samsung Electronics. However, China's YMTC moved up to third place in the second quarter of 2026, according to Counterpoint Research.
Article Summary: SK Hynix is reportedly seeking US approval to expand its China operations. The South Korean memory chipmaker wants Washington’s permission to export additional US-made semiconductor manufacturing equipment to its Dalian facility. The request comes as Washington works to limit China's access to semiconductor technology.
